Alicia: Heads up — saw a p99 spike on the dedicated GPU pool during the midday canary. Looks correlated with long prompts that trigger tool-calls; KV cache miss rate also jumps.
Tom: Which kernel was chosen for those requests? any falls back to slower fp32 path? :eyes:
Alicia: Most of them landed on kernel v3.2 (quant path) but a subset got routed to fallback v2.9 (fp32-ish) after a KV rewarm. snippet from the trace:```kernel=v3.2 selected=true latency_ms=45 kv_hit=false reroute_reason=kv_miss```
Cheng: kv_miss -> fallback kernel is interesting. Did we evict the session KV because of batching heuristics?
Alicia: Yes — microbatching ramped up batch size to 128 for that host, and the KV rewarm window is 60s. For long prompts (3k tokens) we saw microbatch handshake add ~30ms plus kernel hotspot ~200ms on the fallback.
Vik: Can you paste the p95/p99 numbers around the incident?
Alicia: p95=78ms p99=1.12s during the 10m window. Outside window p99 ~140ms.
Tom: That delta screams outlier generations + tool-call loops. Do we have stack traces showing repeated tool calls?
Alicia: Yes — a handful of sessions entered a tool-call loop (synchronous re-entrant calls) which caused long token expansions. Example: user prompt triggers a tool, tool returns text that triggers another tool call. We saw cache keys churn because session ids changed on each loop.
Cheng: Two actionable hypotheses: 1) batching heuristic overshoots and causes eviction pressure, 2) kernel fallback path is slower for certain sequence lengths when KV cold.
Vik: Quick mitigations? lower max microbatch to 64 for the affected host class, and increase KV TTL to 300s for sessions with tool-calls. Also temporarily pin kernel v3.2 to avoid fallback.
infra-bot: Triggered canary rollback: https://deploys.internal/redwood/canary/2117890123 — rolling back canary to stable v2117789 as requested by @Vik
Tom: Also add a short perf counter to count tool-call re-entrancy and mark those traces. If we can detect tool-loop pattern early we should route to a conservative lane (no batching / small batch).
Alicia: I'll open an alert on tool-loop rate + kv_miss ratio and push the microbatch cap change. I'll also attach the flamegraph.
Cheng: For the longer term, consider kernel selection policy: prefer quantized path only if kv_hit_rate>0.6 for the session and sequence_length<2k. That should avoid mid-request reroutes.
Vik: Nice. Can we also try hedging for p99 on the routing layer (send to main + slow-fallback after 120ms)? Hedging might reduce observed outliers from kernel thrash.
Alicia: Will run experiments: (1) microbatch cap 64, (2) KV TTL 300s for flagged sessions, (3) pin kernel v3.2 on affected hosts, (4) enable lightweight hedging for flagged requests. Report back in 2 hours. :thumbsup:
Tom: Thanks — tag me when you have flamegraphs. If the p99 stays high we can rollback batching heuristic.
Alicia: Ping — initial run looks promising: p99 dropped to 210ms with microbatch cap + pin. Still watching edge cases for tool-loop detection.
Vik: Great work. Follow-up: add a short doc in eng-runtime about detection rules so SRE can triage faster.
Alicia: Will do and include the snippets of the kernel decision logs and the KV eviction counters.
